title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a draft of the comparison between de Rham cohomology and singular (constant-sheaf) cohomology. Here X is a (presumably C^infty or analytic) manifold and k = R or C. The surrounding cote is about the divided-power de Rham complex. The neighbouring 'pages' are typescript of SGA 7 Exp. IX (Néron models, component groups ₙΦ, ₙΨ), which serves as scrap paper (verso) and is unrelated to this page.

The objects are:
- Ω* is the de Rham complex, with augmentation k → Ω*.
- S_X^* is the sheaf of singular cochains, the sheafification of U ↦ C^*(S(U)_*, k).
- S'_X^* is the analogous sheaf built on a restricted class of simplices S(X)' (presumably smooth simplices).
- Both singular cochain sheaves are resolutions of k (augmentations ε_S, ε_{S'}) and are 'homotopiquement fins' (homotopically fine).
- Hence, by Cartan's theorem, Γ(X, S_X^*) → RΓ(X, S_X^*) is a quasi-isomorphism, and similarly for S'.

The first (struck-out) diagram tries to line up RΓ(X,k) ≃ RΓ(X,S^*) ≃ Γ(X,S^*) = C^*(S(X),k) with the corresponding primed row and RΓ(X,Ω*). It is abandoned.

The NB then states the key point. A formula (4) together with k_* defines a homomorphism of complexes of sheaves Ω* → S'_X^*. The circled label on the arrow is most plausibly 'intégr.', i.e. integration of forms over smooth simplices, with Stokes giving compatibility with d. This map is compatible with the augmentations from k, so the square k → Ω*, k → S'^*, Ω* → S'^* commutes in D(X).

This yields a commutative cube:
- The top layer consists of global sections: C^*(X,Ω*) → C^*(X,S'^*) = C(S'_X,k), with [C(X,k)] dashed to C^*(X,S^*) = C(S_X,k).
- The bottom layer consists of the RΓ's: RΓ(X,Ω*) → RΓ(X,S'^*), and RΓ(X,k) → RΓ(X,S^*).
- The vertical maps are quasi-isomorphisms by Cartan (homotopically fine sheaves) and by the hypothesis on S'.

The base of the cube consists of isomorphisms, since it is RΓ applied to a square of isomorphisms in a derived category; this rests on Ω*, S^*, S'^* all being resolutions of k. A two-out-of-three argument then shows the remaining face consists of isomorphisms. The conclusion is that the integration map C^*(X,Ω*) → C^*(S'(X),k) is a quasi-isomorphism inducing the canonical de Rham isomorphism, and it is compatible with RΓ(X,k).

This is the classical sheaf-theoretic proof of the de Rham theorem (Weil–Cartan–Godement style). It is presumably being used as the model or real-case benchmark for the divided-power de Rham comparison.
errors: No real error. The 'two-out-of-three' step for the remaining faces is stated loosely ('car on le sait déjà pour deux autres') but is correct for a commutative square in which three of the four arrows are isomorphisms.
The integration map is only additive (not multiplicative) at cochain level. That is irrelevant here, since only the additive comparison is claimed.

ideas.what: Sheaf-theoretic de Rham theorem: integration map Ω* → sheaf of smooth singular cochains, compatible with augmentations, plus Cartan's theorem on homotopically fine sheaves, gives de Rham ≃ singular cohomology via a commutative cube in the derived category.
ideas.modern_name: de Rham theorem via sheaf resolutions / integration quasi-isomorphism
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Rham (1931); sheaf proof by Weil, H. Cartan (Séminaire Cartan 1950–51), Godement
ideas.where_published: Standard (Séminaire Cartan, Godement, Bredon); not a Grothendieck result

ideas.what: Use of 'homotopically fine' sheaves of singular cochains so that global sections compute RΓ

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of the classical de Rham comparison isomorphism, presumably as a model for the divided-power case. Nothing new or uncredited. The SGA 7 IX typescript on adjacent pages is just recycled paper.
transcription_corrections: The circled label on the arrow Ω* → S'_X^* most likely reads 'intégr.' (integration), not 'homot. [?]'.
'La [?] lettre (4)' is more plausibly 'la relation (4)' / 'la formule (4)' jointe avec k_*.

In the cube, the diagonal arrow into C^*(X,S'^*_X) is labelled '≃ hyp. sur S'_X' (quasi-iso by hypothesis on S'), and the vertical arrow C(S_X,k) → RΓ(X,S_X^*) is labelled '2 (Cartan, S_X^* étant "homot. fine")'.
The neighbouring pages (SGA 7 Exp. IX typescript, pp. 457–458) are versos/scrap paper, unrelated to this page's content.
